NAME: Uncertainty-aware graph convolutional neural network for vibrational free‑energy prediction
TYPE: method

DIRECT_CLAIMS: A graph convolutional neural network predicts vibrational free energies with root‑mean‑square errors of 8.23 meV/atom (training), 11.34 meV/atom (validation) and 12.31 meV/atom (test), and its predictions for MgS and NaH polymorphs match DFT‑computed values across the 200–700 K range.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: Screening of approximately 50 000 inorganic crystals with the machine‑learning model identified over 2 000 temperature‑induced solid‑solid polymorphic transitions between 300 K and 600 K, including 130 stable transitions within the technologically relevant 300 K–350 K interval.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: Twenty‑one stable polar‑nonpolar transitions are predicted to exhibit relative lattice‑thermal‑conductivity changes of at least 20 % (0.20), ranging up to a 73 % increase for ZrSeO with a conductivity ratio of 1.73.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: Several predicted solid‑solid transitions show large entropy changes exceeding 300 J K⁻¹ kg⁻¹ (e.g., Li₃MnF₇: 342.3 J K⁻¹ kg⁻¹, PnCl₂: 338.3 J K⁻¹ kg⁻¹, Fe₄OF₇: 252.1 J K⁻¹ kg⁻¹), while the highest entropy changes (> 400 J K⁻¹ kg⁻¹) are limited to transitions above 450 K and occur exclusively in nonpolar‑nonpolar categories, reducing their relevance for room‑temperature applications.
ARTICLE: Machine Learning-Guided Discovery of Temperature-Induced Solid-Solid Phase Transitions in Inorganic Materials

NAME: High‑throughput screening
TYPE: technique
DIRECT_CLAIMS: After fine‑tuning, CHGNet serves as a data‑efficient model for high‑precision simulations across diverse chemistries, supporting high‑throughput screening efforts.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: High‑throughput screening of 188,722 GeNOME crystals with the universal model identifies 21,973 insulators (3,940 direct‑gap) and 5,109 flat‑band materials, nearly doubling the entries in the Materials Flatband Database.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: High‑throughput screening identified TiP, LiSiNi₂, and CoSi₂ as the most promising Li‑ion battery anode conversion reactions, offering high capacity, moderate voltage, and low volume expansion.

NAME: Frozen-framework potential energy surface (PES) descriptor screening
TYPE: method

DIRECT_CLAIMS: The frozen-framework PES descriptor screening ranks lithium-containing Materials Project compounds such that eight of the ten highest‑ranked materials are confirmed to be room‑temperature superionic conductors by first‑principles calculations.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: The proposed screening method is approximately 50 × faster than molecular dynamics driven by a machine‑learning interatomic potential and at least 3 000 × faster than first‑principles molecular dynamics.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: The combined descriptor Ξ, defined as the product of sigmoid‑transformed connected and disconnected free‑volume descriptors at a 0.5 eV threshold, achieves higher ranking scores than each individual descriptor and far exceeds random‑guess performance.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: Free‑volume (FV) descriptors evaluated at energy thresholds between 0.3 eV and 0.5 eV consistently outperform or match the minimal percolation energy (MPE) descriptor across all three evaluation scores.

NAME: Materials Project
TYPE: method

DIRECT_CLAIMS: The Materials Project database contains computed structural, electronic, and energetic data for over 33,000 inorganic compounds, generated using more than 15 million CPU‑hours of computation.
DIRECT_CLAIMS: The Materials Project provides an open RESTful API and a high‑level Python library (pymatgen) that enable programmatic querying and analysis of the full dataset.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: Visual warnings are displayed on the Materials Project website for compounds whose calculated oxidation states, cell volumes, or bond lengths deviate significantly from experimental norms, helping users assess data reliability.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: Using Materials Project tools, researchers designed a new class of sodium‑based carbonophosphate compounds, predicted them to be thermodynamically stable, synthesized them hydrothermally, and experimentally confirmed their Li‑ion battery performance after ion exchange.
ARTICLE: Machine Learning-Guided Discovery of Temperature-Induced Solid-Solid Phase Transitions in Inorganic Materials

NAME: two-step supervised-unsupervised melting temperature prediction with symbolic regression
TYPE: method
DIRECT_CLAIMS: A curated dataset of 476 binary ionic compound melting temperatures spanning 0-4,000°C was compiled for machine learning model development.
DIRECT_CLAIMS: The best one-step gradient-boosted tree regression model achieves 165±4 K MAE and 0.89 R² on the test set for melting temperature prediction.
DIRECT_CLAIMS: A two-step approach combining unsupervised clustering with supervised regression achieves 156±4 K MAE and 0.92 R², outperforming direct one-step supervised learning.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: Cluster 1 (198 compounds, mostly ionic halides and oxides) achieves 136±5 K MAE and 0.92 R², while Cluster 2 (222 compounds, mostly covalent carbides and nitrides) achieves 189±7 K MAE and 0.90 R².
